subject: Climate & Environment
title: Agricultural Ammonia
description: A quick win: understand Agricultural Ammonia.

hook.text: Farms produce a pollutant you rarely hear about: ammonia. And it is everywhere.

buildup.text: Livestock waste and synthetic fertilizers release ammonia gas into the air constantly.

discovery.text: Ammonia reacts with other pollutants in the atmosphere to form fine particulate matter.

twist.text: In parts of Europe, farming is the single biggest source of PM2.5 — more than traffic.

climax.text: Reducing ammonia is tricky because it means changing how billions of animals are fed and housed.

punchline.text: The farm next door may pollute your air more than the highway.

quiz.question: What does ammonia form when it reacts with other pollutants?

details.summary: Agriculture is the dominant source of ammonia emissions, primarily from livestock waste and synthetic fertilizer application. Ammonia reacts in the atmosphere to form fine particulate matter, making farming a surprisingly large contributor to poor air quality.
details.whyItMatters: Ammonia from farms drifts into cities and forms PM2.5, linking agricultural practice directly to urban health. It is one of the least regulated major air pollutants.
takeaways: Livestock manure and urea fertilizer are top ammonia sources
Ammonia reacts with acids in the air to form PM2.5 particles
Precision fertilizer application can cut ammonia loss significantly

faq.question: How does ammonia from farms become urban particle pollution?
faq.answer: Ammonia gas rises from fields and livestock operations, travels hundreds of kilometers, and reacts with sulfuric and nitric acids in the atmosphere. The resulting ammonium sulfate and nitrate particles are a major component of PM2.5 in many cities.

faq.question: What farming practices reduce ammonia emissions?
faq.answer: Injecting fertilizer below the soil surface, covering manure storage, adjusting livestock diets, and applying fertilizer in cool, calm conditions all reduce ammonia volatilization by 30 to 70 percent.
